causal_interpretation: A single real X11Backend.capture call returned with a complete 1920x1080 PNG (2,506,957 bytes) already present; this rules out a general compositor delay or a permanently invalid path.

Two concurrent real X11Backend.capture calls used the same exact gnome-screenshot -f argv. In r1 one target was absent at X11Backend.capture's immediate chmod and materialized later; the other remained absent. In r2 both calls returned with only 86-byte PNG headers, then both files asynchronously grew to complete 1920x1080 PNGs.

The D-Bus service file declares org.gnome.Screenshot as the single-instance --gapplication-service. The live service status captured during the first probe identified /usr/bin/gnome-screenshot --gapplication-service. Concurrent clients therefore share one screenshot service and can observe queued/partial output after the short-lived CLI process exits.

The retained strace shows each CLI process execve and exits 0 before the r2 target files reached final size; no stderr was emitted. This distinguishes asynchronous output completion under concurrent single-instance dispatch from a subprocess failure.

No helper/source change is justified by this diagnosis yet. The narrow production repair surface is to wait for the exact expected output file to exist and pass complete-image validation after gnome-screenshot returns, within the existing capture deadline, while retaining the same identity and argv. A future fix should also serialize calls if the service contract requires one request at a time; do not add an alternate capture backend or widen freshness bounds.
diagnosis: gnome-screenshot is a D-Bus GApplication single-instance service and returns before its output file is durably complete
